notes: WORKING ROUTE: robots.txt 200 permissive (only /wp-admin/, /*?s=, /wp-content/boost-cache/ disallowed; no Crawl-delay) advertises https://www.lapresse.tn/sitemap_index.xml -> 200, a Yoast sitemapindex of 50 children. The post urlsets are post-sitemap.xml, post-sitemap2.xml ... post-sitemap42.xml, each ~1000 posts, and the HIGHEST NUMBER IS THE NEWEST (lastmod: post-sitemap42=2026-10-27, 41=2026-10-14, 40=2026-09-28, 39=2026-09-13), so the whole month sits in 40/41/42 (4 requests, 12s). The script reads the index and picks children whose lastmod >= 2026-09-20 (plus the highest-numbered one) instead of hard-coding numbers. DATE: every post URL is /YYYY/MM/DD/slug/ and that segment equals the page JSON-LD datePublished and <meta article:published_time> exactly (11 pages re-fetched across 2026-09-25..10-25: 200, 2537-6427 chars of visible text, datePublished identical to the listed day, e.g. 2026-10-10T17:29:48+00:00). <lastmod> is the MODIFIED stamp (drifts a day or more) so it is only a fallback for a loc without a dated path (0 such cases here). RESULT: 1893 unique URLs, 31/31 days, 2026-09-30=59, 2026-10-10=76, 2026-10-20=53 (min 50 on 10-13). TRAPS: (1) the advertised /news-sitemap.xml is only ~2 days of recent posts - do NOT build a month from it; (2) the old attempt that produced 700 URLs over 19 days with 09-30=0 and 10-10=1 clearly came off that news sitemap; (3) some entries in file 42 carry older path dates (2026-09-05, 09-16) because those posts were edited, so always filter on the PATH date, never on lastmod.
